utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. This is case number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic, Dragan Jokic, and Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before we have the witness, is there anything that both parties would like to bring to the attention to this Trial Chamber? Yes. Yes, please. MS. DE LA TORRE: Nothing from the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about from the Defence? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Nothing from the Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just like to ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And good afternoon. It's nice to be here in the afternoon. It appears that the Prosecution is going to attempt to admit into evidence all the exhibits used by this witness, Mr. Ruez. And I would ask that since we just received their list of their intention today, that instead of making a ruling on it, let Defence counsel review it tonight and we can approve or lodge our objections in the morning, if that's okay with the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Usually we'll have the parties' intents of the documents which will admitted for the present witness after the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Wilson.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Nothing from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Shall we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest during the weekend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have the Serbo-Croatian version in the -- yes, I had. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. You may proceed, Ms. De la Torre. MS. DE LA TORRE: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. De la Torre: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, when we left on Friday, the Court viewed a videotape that you had taken of the scene in Kravica when you were first able to visit that particular location. If you recall back on Friday, in look at Prosecution Exhibit 10.3, we enlarged a window on the warehouse in order for you to point out the number of bullet holes that were present at that time. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I would just correct the fact that I am not the one who filmed this videotape. It was filmed by our colleague named Peter Nicholson.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present when that videotape was taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was present with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you present on the scene for that scene investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Referring back to the window that was enlarged in order for you to identify the number of pockmarks or bullet holes in it, we're now going to show you what we've marked as Prosecution Exhibit 10.10, a clip of videotape taken by Zoran Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Once again I would like to object to any video footage by Zoran Petrovic because it has been stated by the witness, Mr. Ruez, in prior testimony that Mr. Petrovic edited his footage and didn't turn over all the footage to the Prosecution. So it's a one-sided picture that we're -- we're viewing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think you raised this issue at the very beginning, and this Trial Chamber made the ruling that we'll watch that part of the picture, the footage, and then the Prosecutor will ask some questions to this witness concerning the certain amendments and cuttage of these footnotes, if we could get the proper answer. Then we'll decide whether to admit them into evidence or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's watch that video footage. MS. DE LA TORRE: And for the record, Your Honour, I misspoke. It's actually Prosecution Exhibit 21.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: MS. DE LA TORRE:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going back, Mr. Ruez, to the shot of Prosecution Exhibit 10.3, we'll enlarge that window again to refresh the Court's recollection. Can you explain to the Court the comparison that you made between that particular clip of footage and the photograph labelled "10.3"?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So when -- when looking at the previous footage, if we made a stop of -- a still picture of the window, that is, the one at the left of the right part of the building, where the large entrance is, with parts of it destroyed on the right hand of it, so the window at the left of this entrance, on this photograph, one can see that there are several bullet holes just underneath this window. One can count on this one six -- six holes, if not counting three which seem to be really at the bottom of the wall. On the previous video that was filmed 13 July, one could see when stopping the film on this window that there are no traces under the window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did that indicate to you, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When viewing the live footage of Zoran Petrovic, one can see dead bodies outside the warehouse, people who tried to get out. One can also hear the soundtrack where shooting can be heard. But from that video no one can say this shooting is connected with the event seen on the film since it could also be sounds of combat activity occurring between the asphalt road and the hills, or one could also think that it could be what is so-called happy fire, so people shooting in the air just to celebrate something. When one notices that in fact due to the traces on the wall it could very well be that this execution in fact is still ongoing, since later on, after the footage of Zoran Petrovic, there are additional traces of impact on the wall. And this is also consistent with what the survivors of this place told us, since they describe an execution that happened in several waves, not only in one single event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on to Prosecution Exhibit 11.1, Mr. Ruez, there is a colour photograph of a site called Glogova. Can you explain to the Court the connection between the Kravica warehouse and the site at Glogova.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We know from one survivor who was inside the warehouse after the killings occurred that heavy equipment was then used to -- to enter this -- this warehouse. He managed to leave the place before being collected by this heavy equipment, but that indicates that that day probably a cleaning process of that warehouse started, and this was probably completed the following day. At approximately 7 kilometres of Kravica, when going in the direction of Bratunac, is an area of a destroyed village named Glogova, and this is the area where the bodies of those who were killed at the Kravica warehouse have been transported to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 11.2. Were you able to obtain photographic evidence that supported the theory that Glogova was created around the time of the Kravica warehouse massacre?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We obtained an aerial imagery of the village of Glogova dated 5 July that shows a little dirt road, in between this road houses, and the terrain does not show traces of disturbance the 5th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on to Prosecution Exhibit 11.3. There is another aerial image dated 17 July. Could you describe the difference between this photograph and the one dated 5 July.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This one dated 17 July 1995 shows a larger area of this village, Glogova. On this one, one can see the asphalt road that to the right of the picture leads to Bratunac and at the left leads towards Kravica. The bend on the road that leads to the site and the previous photograph was a close shot of a grouping of houses at the left of the picture, bottom left. On this picture one can see that there are two areas of destroyed -- disturbed soil on each side of the little dirt path. Also, a blow-up of the bend of the road that connects the dirt road to the asphalt road is a blow-up of a machine that was initially labelled on the picture that was provided by state department as being digging equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based upon the information that you obtained from these photographs, was an exhumation conducted at this site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, an exhumation was conducted there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was evidence uncovered that linked the massacre at Kravica warehouse with the graves at Glogova?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. The details of the connections will be made during the testimony of my colleague Dean Manning. But as an example, one of the most compelling connection was the metal frame of a door through which the prisoners entered the warehouse, and this frame was broken by the equipment that entered that warehouse. Pieces of masonry and that door frame were later found at the Glogova site inside a mass grave. I also have to point out that at the opposite of the previous mass grave sites we already presented, this one has later on been disturbed, so the result of the exhumation on this site, in terms of number of bodies, does not reflect the number of victims of the Kravica warehouse, since the bodies that have been exhumed in -- exhumed in these sites have later on been relocated in remote areas in order to scatter these bodies in multiple graves and hide the evidence. And all these other sites are not yet -- all of them are not yet exhumed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I am going to have to object to the narrative form of the answer. If you could please instruct the Prosecutor and the witness to leave it to question-and-answer form, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, we have come across this issue last week. I said that if the Prosecutor would like to ask more information, she will put the question to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And on the other hand, Ms. De la Torre, try to lead your witness rather than led him try to do the otherwise. MS. DE LA TORRE: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, despite the violation of the graves at Glogova that you previously mentioned, do you -- were you able to obtain a number of the bodies that were ultimately uncovered at Glogova?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The minimum number of individuals exhumed so far in Glogova is 90 bodies in a site labelled "Glogova V," and 187 bodies in a site named "Glogova II," if it is connected with a secondary site found in an area named Zeleni Jadar. So that is the number -- minimum number of individuals exhumed from that site or who have been at one point at that site at the year 2000. But the exhumations are not over on this topic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, at this time I'd like to go back to Prosecution Exhibit 21, the video that was interrupted on Friday, and finish with the remainder of the film which deals with the activity along the road, Kravica to Konjevic Polje, that you had discussed, as well as the trek of the column.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is on the meadow of Sandici. This is the meadow of Sandici with a group of prisoners on the meadow. This is a stretch of road in the area of Lolici, going to Sandici. Here you can see a Serb soldier wearing a blue helmet on this picture. In the vicinity is a person whose name is General Borovcanin and who is the deputy of the special police brigade, who was in this area of Sandici. This is the bank on the meadow of Sandici. Here the prisoner is passing next to the two-storey destroyed building. He's going to cross now the asphalt road. This is just in front of the building where the truck of abandoned belonging is, and behind is the valley from which the people went down. Here they cross the asphalt road before going on the meadow. This is a return to Potocari area. This is the window with -- with which one can compare the -- the shape of the wall under the window when compared with a photograph dated early 1996. And here is the bus that could be seen on the aerial imagery that was shown previously as well. Sorry, I interrupted. Just to back off of this last comment the bus that we see on the film is not parked exactly on the same location than the one seen on the aerial photograph. The one on the photograph is more at the left of this warehouse. Sorry. These are pictures of the arrival of a column in Nezuk, the group of armed people who managed to break the lines.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] My father got killed, and my uncle. My nephew. They killed my three brothers and my father. We'll probably go. We'll be moving on. You won't stay here long. You'll rest a bit here, refresh a bit, and then you'll go. What's the matter with you? Show a bit of humane behaviour. Do you have a thread of humanity? Do you know approximately how many of you left Srebrenica? From Srebrenica, 40.000. How many remained on the road? Usually I was walking at the head of the column. The 284th Brigade went mostly behind the people who were at the head of the column, behind the Brdski Battalion and the Pistarska Brigade, so we would usually walk behind them. And so I'm not sure about a final number. How many times were you ambushed? How many ambushes did they set for you? Two. Two real ambushes and this action, while breaking through, because the Chetniks did not want to negotiate some sort of peace passage with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. First, I noted that -- that when it comes to the Serbs speaking, including some of the vulgarity that is being used, they -- the Prosecution has no problem and -- inserting that into the footage. Yet here when the Muslims are speaking, for some reason it's not included. I just want to record to reflect that. I don't know why that has happened. I'm sure there's a good explanation. Secondly, just for a point of clarification, the witness indicated after seeing a particular -- what he called soldier with a blue hat -- a blue helmet. In that particular scene he characterised him as a soldier. Perhaps there can be some clarification as how this particular witness knows that that was a soldier and not somebody from MUP, the civilian police, especially since in that particular frame Mr. Borovcanin is seen. Perhaps I'm mistaken, but perhaps he can add some clarification to that. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, they are very good questions. But I think they are probably proper to ask during your cross-examination. We will see whether Ms. De la Torre would like to ask this question or not, so we could have a clearer picture of these issues. MS. DE LA TORRE: With regard to the transcript of the tape, there is an entire transcript of the tape that is available to both the Court and the Defence. With regard to Mr. Karnavas's question concerning the individual on the road, I believe he could properly ask that question during his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, when we left your testimony on Friday, you had prisoners who were detained on the meadow at Sandici, detained on the meadow at Nova Kasaba, and detained in the White House in Potocari. Based upon your investigation, do you know where those prisoners were taken from those detention sites?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As we already said, those who were separated in Potocari, as soon as the 12 were taken to Bratunac town, the same happened with those who were leaving Potocari and were separated in Potocari the 13th. They went through the same process, first to the White House, in front of UN headquarters, and from there they were transported to Bratunac town. The prisoners who were on various fields and meadows in the area between Kravica and Nova Kasaba were also transported towards Bratunac town at the end of the day 13 July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Ruez, it's difficult, given the maps that we are using that are quite enlarged, but can you give the Court an indication of how far Potocari, Nova Kasaba football field, and Sandici meadow are from Bratunac town?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Potocari is very nearby. Bratunac, it's approximately 3 kilometres from Bratunac town. For the rest, the -- the longest distance is the distance between Bratunac and Nova Kasaba, and this would be approximately 20 kilometres from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 12.1, this is an aerial photograph of Bratunac town where you have indicated some of the key sites to which you will be referring. Can you describe for the Court, Mr. Ruez, how big of a town Bratunac is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can hardly describe Bratunac town. I've been there several times. But I cannot give any estimate regarding the population. It's a small -- it's a small town, approximately 2 kilometres north-south and the same east-west. It's not a big town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the aerial photograph marked 12.1, in the lower right-hand corner you have marked the Bratunac Brigade headquarters yes. Yes. This building is indeed of the Kaolin factory, which was a ceramics factory, and this was the location of the Bratunac Brigade in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To give the Court a sense of scale, can you give them an idea of how far it is from the Bratunac Brigade headquarters to the Hotel Fontana, for example, that was depicted in the videotape the Court watched previously?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that the prisoners who were detained in Potocari, Sandici, and Nova Kasaba were transported to sites in Bratunac. Have you marked those on this particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry, I'll rectify my previous answer. I was misoriented on this photograph. The Hotel Fontana is 400 metres away from that -- from that Bratunac Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going back to my next question. The sites that you indicated where prisoners were held, are those marked on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you detail them for the Court?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, only three buildings, as far as we know, have been used to store prisoners during these days in Bratunac. They are all located in the same part of the town, which is close to the centre. If we -- if we could make a blow-up of -- yes, to the left of this blow-up, three buildings. In fact, it is a school complex. One is the Vuk Karadzic School. Behind this school is a large hangar, damaged during the war. This was the first location used to store the prisoners who were coming from Potocari. And next to this hangar is another big building, which is called the Old school. That's how the people refer to it. It was a technical school. These are the three buildings that were used to detain prisoners. And we -- we have survivors from the Old School and from the hangar, but we have no survivor who experienced having stayed in the Vuk Karadzic School there, only indirect witnesses of the presence of prisoners in this place -- I mean, indirect witnesses, as far as victims are concerned, not Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from the witnesses who themselves detailed their detention in these particular sites, Mr. Ruez, how else were you able to identify these three sites as having been holding sites for prisoners?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: By talking with officials of Bratunac town. As an example, talking with Mr. Miroslav Deronjic, the president of the SDS of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: If I might interrupt just for a second. I would like re-urge my running objection that I put on the record yesterday, that he is testifying from witnesses who it's evident will not be called to testify here at the trial and that clearly violates the ruling under Milosevic. But I won't object again. Just every time he mentions a witness who is not coming to testify, I would like for my objection to be marked on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this minute we still don't know if those people mentioned will come to testify or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sure Deronjic won't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. But the answer is very clear. The information he got is by talking with some officials of that town. Maybe Ms. De la Torre could indicate whether those people will testify here or not. MS. DE LA TORRE: I could perhaps clarify, Your Honour, with a subsequent question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please. MS. DE LA TORRE:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, was the information you received concerning these particular holding or detention sites from Muslim victims corroborated through interviews with Serb witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to determine during the course of your investigation when the first prisoners began to arrive in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We know that from one survivor, who was separated in Potocari, taken to the White House in Potocari first, and from there that day - that was the 12th July 1995 - he was taken to an unidentified location that he later on confirmed being that hangar once he was shown photographs of this building. He recognised this building as being the one he had been held into. So July 12th for the use of this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you able to determine when approximately the last prisoners were sent or deported from Bratunac towards the north?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The evacuation of the town from all the prisoners who were kept in the town started very early morning of 14 July. In fact, around midnight by the end of the day of 13th. And the last prisoners who left the -- who left Bratunac town were the ones detained at the Old School. We can have a certainty about this from the declarations of one survivor of the Branjevo Farm who was taken from the old school to the Pilica School on July 15. MS. DE LA TORRE: And for the record, Your Honour, the survivors from Branjevo Farm, for the Defence counsel's reference, are number 69, P105; number 70, P113; and number 71, P116.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, approximately how far from the Bratunac Brigade headquarters is the hangar where the first prisoners began to arrive in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would give approximately the same estimate I gave previously, a bit more than 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the Vuk Karadzic school? How far is that from the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these locations from in the same area of the town. They are next to each another. The old school and the hangar, the Vuk Karadzic School are in the same area, the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to obtain an estimate of approximately how many prisoners were detained between the 12th and 15th in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On these figures, the only estimate I would personally rely on would be the final count of the victims that we will exhume from all the exhumations that have been and still need to be conducted. Only that final number, minimum number of individuals, will enable us to have an idea of how many people were also detained in Bratunac during these days, since as far as we know, all the people who have been detained in that location ultimately ended up dead except those who came here to testify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based upon the information that you obtained during the course of your investigation, would you put the number of prisoners held in these three detention sites in the thousands?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So based on your testimony, Mr. Ruez, am I correct in saying that the night of the 12th there were thousands of prisoners, approximately in your estimation, 4 to 500 metres from the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. By the end of the 12th, only a few hundred were -- were in Bratunac town. It's by the end of the 13th that the town was -- that all these prisoners were hold in various places in Bratunac town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based upon the information you obtained, prisoners were transported to Bratunac all day on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as we know, yes. Though, we also know from one witness who I think is coming to testify during this trial, who is a Serb soldier - am I correct if I say that he's coming? - I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a bit difficult, because I don't know exactly who you're referring to. However, let me just put it this way: You indicated that by the end of the 13th there were thousands of prisoners in Bratunac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the day of the 14th? Did the deportations then begin from Bratunac to the north?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did. The first prisoners who left the town were those who had spent the night between 13th and 14th, onboard of buss and trucks lined in the streets of Bratunac town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that there were some people who were kept on buses. Were you able to ascertain why it was that some were pus on buses or left on buses, as opposed to being put in the three locations you've previously identified?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's only an assumption that since the three buildings I already mentioned were at full capacity, the other prisoners stayed onboard of buss and trucks, probably because there were no other buildings in that town who were ready to -- I mean, who could be used to keep prisoners inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The information that you obtained about individuals being held on buses, were you able to corroborate that -- those particular pieces of information from Muslim survivors as well as DutchBat soldiers who were kept in this particular area during this time?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct. We have an -- an idea of where these lines of buss and trucks were parked in Bratunac town, both from the accounts of victims who were onboard of these vehicles but also from Dutch witnesses who could see them in the streets when they were moving. An example, to go to -- from the Hotel Fontana to -- to sustain themselves at the Bratunac Brigade canteen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the three sites where thousands of prisoners were held approximate 500 metres from the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, Mr. Ruez, I noticed that you indicated directly in front of the Bratunac Brigade headquarters a bus.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We know about the -- the presence of that bus from the testimony of a Dutch UN soldier who spotted that bus filled with male prisoners just in front of Bratunac Brigade headquarters. That was the 13th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in addition to the prisoners who were held nearby in the schools, there were also prisoners on buses directly in front of the Bratunac Brigade headquarters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on, Mr. Ruez --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. I believe we went from a bus to buses. This is a conclusion now that is being formulated by the Prosecutor. If he has some testimony that buses, as opposed to a particular bus, I would like to hear that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- well, Mr. Karnavas, I don't think the Prosecutor is talking about from bus to buses. She's talking about the distance from those buses to that brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It was established through the Prosecutor that according to a Dutch Battalion soldier, that a bus was parked in front of there. But then the characterisation, if you note very carefully the way she phrases the question, she's looping. She'll take part of the answer, form it into part of her next question. So it went from a bus to buses. That's a characterisation in my opinion from her, not from the witness. Now, if the witness has independent knowledge that buses were in front of the Bratunac Brigade, very well, Your Honour. I don't have a problem with that. She can elicit the question from the witness, as opposed to making the assumption in prefacing her -- her next question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Prosecutor, you might ask some questions to this witness to make these things more clear for us. MS. DE LA TORRE:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez -- MS. DE LA TORRE: Well, for the record, Your Honour, I believe that these are matters, again that, are more properly dealt with during the course of Mr. Karnavas's cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, Mr. Ruez, there is indicated on this particular aerial photograph the word "bus," which you placed on this photograph. Now, reviewing your testimony that you gave moments ago, did you receive information from DutchBat witnesses in the course of your investigation that Muslim prisoners were held on a bus directly in front of the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm it is yes. And the reason why this -- this specific label is "bus," only one bus, is because the witness in this specific instance only mentions one vehicle, versus in the other situations where I labelled these convoys buses it is because we are talking about more than one vehicle. In fact, we don't know exactly how many vehicles we are talking about, since those who were onboard of these buses generally could see only vehicles in front and vehicles behind, but they didn't know how long the line of vehicles was in the street. So it's several buses, when it is written "buses,", with an "S," but in this instance it is only one bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving on to the next execution site, Mr. Ruez, are we now moving from sites which are generally referred to has being in the south to sites that are in the north?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court the distinction that is made as an investigator between the southern sites and the northern sites?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We separate these areas for two reasons, in fact; one being because they are both part of a separate geographical block, if one can say so. The area south is -- is separate from the area north -- from a significant distance, which is approximately 40 kilometres minimum, between 40 and 70 for the sites who are the more north. And the two areas are very separate geographically. You -- you go through the canyon of the Drinjaca before entering the Drina Valley that leads to Zvornik. It's two very different type of -- of landscapes and areas. And the reason why also we split this large crime scene at 70 kilometres from north to south and 40 kilometres from east to west in two zones is because of the process which has been used to exterminate these people. We make a difference between the events that happened south, dated 12 and 13 July, and then we enter in another phase of the killings, which happened elsewhere in a much more organised process during the days of 14 and 15, 16 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning your attention, Mr. Ruez, to the first of what you've identified as the northern sites. I'll show you what's been marked as Prosecution Exhibit 13.1, a photograph of the school at Grbavci. MS. DE LA TORRE: For the record, Your Honour, the witnesses who Mr. Ruez may refer to during this particular section who survived this execution are number 64, P108; number 65, P110; and number 66, all of whom are on the Prosecution witness list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, were you present when this particular photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I took this picture in January 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe for the Court how it was that you first identified the Grbavci School as a potential crime scene?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we interviewed the first survivor of the massacre in connection with this final detention site, we got information that it was a school with a gym attached to it and that very nearby where the execution site was was a railroad line. With these two elements, we tried to find out if someone could pinpoint a specific school that had a gym and a railroad track. And the fact is that the Grbavci school, according to a teacher who knew the area and who was met by one of my colleagues at the time, Jos Papen, one teacher said that the only school in the area who had a gym was the Grbavci school. And we also ultimately found a map of the area that marked the railroad line, and indeed this school is close to a railroad line, so we made the assumption that this was the school and we went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you identified this particular location, do you recall when it was that you were first able to visit the crime scene?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We entered very briefly this location in January 1996, but extremely briefly. It was -- it was not a mission designed to -- to spend time observing these places. The first real verifications that we did there was in April 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As part of your investigation, Mr. Ruez, did you have the opportunity to take a survivor back to this location in order to verify that it was indeed where he had been held prior to being taken for execution?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After we went there, we presented first photographs to the victims. But in -- in 1999, we brought the victims back to these -- to these sites, and indeed they recognised that school as being the one. But we didn't enter the school with the victims. The goal was to bring them -- to try to have them bring us, in fact, to the execution site to check if they were able to find it, but they were not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able ascertain when prisoners first began to arrive from Bratunac at the Grbavci school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the survivors who were kept in the gym, the first -- the first ones who arrived, arrived early in the morning. They had left Bratunac town around midnight, and they arrived in the morning at the gym, and the gym was filled in the course of that -- of that morning, until it was at full capacity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 13.2. Could you explain to the Judges what this photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This shows the playground next to the gymnasium. This is where the prisoners had to abandon their belongings that were put in a -- in a stack nearby the -- the entrance, and the survivors later on also recalled having walked through a -- a long fence. And this is the fence that can be seen at the right of the photograph and that leads to the entrance door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 13.3. You have labelled on this photograph an entrance and an exit. What is the particular significance of those two items on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The prisoners entered the gym -- this gym by the door that labelled "entrance." They were then made to sit in rows. And once the gym was full, the process of evacuating the people little group after little group onboard of the truck to bring them to the execution site, they went first through the -- the entrance of the wardrobe that is marked on this photograph "exit." There they were blindfolded. They were given a sip of water before being put onboard of a little TAM truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The description that you were given from the survivors concerning what occurred in the Grbavci school, was that consistent with what you found once you were able to investigate the scene?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are some details that indeed added corroboration to what they -- what they had said in their statements. We have not prepared the exhibits that could show these details. As an example, there are some holes in the ceiling, in the metal ceiling of this gym, and these holes could be consistent with the fact that from time to time soldiers who were guarding these prisoners were reported having shot in the air in order to have the people stay quiet inside. There were also some of these holes on windows of this gym.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also obtain information as to whether or not General Mladic arrived at the scene and addressed the prisoners held in the school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the survivors who was kept in this gym declares that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 13.4. You've labelled the door in the centre of the photograph as the exit. Can you explain to the Court the significance of that particular doorway, vis-a-vis the statements that you obtained from the survivors.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The little construction attached to the gym is the wardrobe I already described. And on this picture one can see the door, which was used to -- for the exit of these prisoners. And immediately there was a little truck that was back towards this door and the people were climbing onboard of this truck in that location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, we have now what's been marked as 13.5, a videotape that was taken at the school. Were you present when this video was taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately when that was?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the helicopter park, and the rest of the film was filmed by my colleague Peter Nicholson who was together with me on that mission at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm sorry, did you say you were present when that videotape was taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. MS. DE LA TORRE: If we can go ahead and play 13.5

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So this is an aerial view from the school with the main building -- Can we have the sound off. That is indeed the entrance. Turning to the right leads to the school building, and to the left to the gymnasium. Here is the gymnasium. At the left here, now the entrance door. And at the right here now the access to the wardrobe. A piece of -- of cloth. We found these other pieces of cloth in a dump site nearby the execution site, and this cloth was used also to blindfold the -- the victims or attach their hands in the back. That same cloth was -- same type of cloth was found in the mass graves during the exhumation. To the left here is a pile of rubbish. We went through this pile of rubbish and lined on the ground the elements of interest that we found among this pile of various rubbish. A number of shell casings. One has to know that the school was used also from time to time by the -- by the army, so these casings are not necessarily linked with the events we are discussing today. We have no reports about people having been killed at this school, or at least not more than one. And mainly, strips of cloth, more than 100, of various colours, textures. We selected a representative sample of these pieces of cloth for further analysis. We -- we kept 12 different types. This is a caterpillar track with pieces of cloth attached to it and knots. We have no specific explanation for this specific object. These are the 12 that were kept ultimately for lab analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And Ms. De la Torre, could we have the break now. MS. DE LA TORRE: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at 4.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can we have the witness, please. You may proceed, Ms. De la Torre. MS. DE LA TORRE: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, you indicated that prisoners were taken from the school and blindfolded. Were you able to ascertain where they were taken to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 13.6. Would you explain to the Court how it was that you identified the locations marked LZ1 and LZ2 as having been connected to the Grbavci school.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to the testimonies of four witnesses who claimed having survived execution after having been detained in that school, the indication we had was that the site -- the execution site was in a quite close vicinity of the school, since they recalled having driven only a short distance from the school to the site. And also one very specific ground feature, that was the vicinity of a railroad that was nearby this execution site. So having narrowed down the possible area where the event might have happened, we made a request of aerial imagery in order to compare the ground in that area before that date and after that date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give the Court an idea of how far it is from the school at Grbavci to the two sites located -- I'm sorry, marked as LZ-1 and LZ-2.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We measured the road from the school to the point of the asphalt road that then becomes a dirt road leading to the site, and that distance was 800 metres by the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were the victims transported from the school to the execution site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were put onboard of a little truck and transported to the site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 13.7. Could you explain to the Court the significance in the difference of the geographic features between LZ-1 and LZ-2 as they relate to the witness testimony?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I just need also to mention that unfortunately on this exhibit we have mislabelled the sites, and that they should be LZ-2 on this picture should be coded LZ-1 so that we keep the same coding when the chief exhumator used during the excavation that was conducted there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For clarity then. If you could just refer to the two sites -- one is marked with a triangle and one is marked with a square on Prosecution Exhibit 13.7. Perhaps that might make things a bit clearer.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So on this picture one can see the asphalt road that is more at the top of the picture. Going to the right leads to the Grbavci school. And here one can see a dirt road that connects this asphalt road to the site where there is the triangle, and the straight line is the railroad. Underneath the railroad is an underpass that enables one to drive from the asphalt road to the site where the triangle-shape site, and this triangle-shaped meadow is the meadow that was used first to commit the executions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Court how it was that you were able to determine that the site marked with a triangle was the killing field that was used first.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because the victims described that at the end of their little trip they were on a bump road, a bumpy road, and this bumpy part of the road is in fact the dirt road that goes from the asphalt road to this meadow. The other indication is that the survivors claimed that at one point the meadow was completely covered with bodies, which is indeed something possible when you are on the ground at the Lazete site that has this triangular shape, and that would be totally impossible had -- had they been talking about the other site where the meadow is extremely large. The -- the other element is also that none of the prisoners who are inside of the gym did report having heard intensive shooting coming from the area. That was quite strange due to the proximity of the site. And one explanation to this is that there is a natural sound barrier created by this railroad that is on an elevation approximately 3 metres high. So this is also something that can limit the sound to travel to the Grbavci school. In addition to that is also the fact that there was some constant noise of people whispering in that -- in that warehouse and also their ears were buzzing because of the shots that were sometimes fired inside this gymnasium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 13.8. You have a photograph here. Could you explain to the Court which of the two sites that were marked on the previous photograph this one represents.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the triangular-shaped meadow, when taking the photograph, standing on the meadow, and looking towards the underpass that then leads to the asphalt road going towards the Grbavci school. That part of the meadow that is just in front is indeed the execution site. The markers -- the yellow markers on the ground spot items that we located on the ground that day. And the area at the top of the picture which is close by a yellow tape line is the area that was designated as the rest area for the execution squad, the place where they were reloading their weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that the yellow markers on this particular photograph represent pieces of evidence that were uncovered at the site. Could you give the Court an indication of the type of evidence that you were able to recover when you visited the site for the first time.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The items that could be found on the surface of the ground on that location were shell casings, bits of clothing, human bones scattered -- scattered on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 13.9. We are now switching from the -- from a view from the ground at that particular site again to an aerial depiction. On this photograph, you've marked both LZ-1, LZ-2, and additionally an underpass and a dump site. Could you explain to the Court the significance of the underpass and the dump site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here the labels are correct. After the execution was over at the Lazete I site. In fact, once the meadow was full -- covered with dead bodies, one of the survivors heard the team leader of the execution squad ordering his men to go to the other site, referred to the other site, and he requested them to take an ammunition box. And for -- to do this, they had to then go through -- through the underpass to go to this second site, which is marked Lazete II. When we searched this area, we also went to a location that is marked "dump site," which is an area approximately 150 metres away from Lazete I and that is -- you can go there walking on a little dirt road. And on that dump site we found various items.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 13.10. Is this a photograph of the dump site you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The dump site is at the left of the picture where a member of the Office of the Prosecutor, Stephanie Frease, is standing. And we searched through that pile of rubbish and lined on the ground items that were discovered there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give the Court an indication of the type of articles that you were able to recover from the dump site.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mainly it was clothing, hats. But the most interesting element that we found there was again a large number of pieces of cloth that we -- we made a sampling of these pieces of cloth according to texture, colour, and these pieces of cloth were then analysed by the Dutch forensic laboratory and connections were later made between this cloth, the cloth found at the school, and the cloth that was found inside the mass graves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned previously that you had requested aerial imagery of the location in order to ascertain whether or not there had been a disturbance. Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 13.11. Does this photograph indeed confirm the fact that there was a disturbance at the location indicated by the witnesses in between the 5th and the 27th of July?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On this -- on the same exhibit we have, in fact, two photographs. At the left is a photograph dated July 5 that shows completely at the left the asphalt road and the straight line is the railroad. And one can see that on the -- on the ground there is no other disturbance than the road, the dirt road, three houses, and this railroad; versus, on 27 July 1995 there are two areas of clear disturbance visible on the ground, the area marked "Lazete II," with a clear disturbance, and also the area marked "Lazete I," that is, the second execution site we -- we talked about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based upon the aerial images and the information and evidence that you were able to obtain during the course of the investigation, was this site exhumed?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And without going into all the particulars, which will come later, can you give the Court an overview of what was discovered when this site was exhumed?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Though -- though that site also was later on disturbed end of September, beginning of October, left over of 493 bodies were still found during the exhumations that were conducted on these two sites from 1996 to 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this time we have Prosecution Exhibit 13.12, a videotape of this particular site.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I have to return on the information I just gave. That number of 493 includes also 200 -- a large amount of -- of that number is in fact bodies that are --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we stop that. That were later found in secondary graves connected with primary these sites. So I don't have the figures, I think, of the bodies who were found at Lazete I and Lazete II. The number I was given was already including secondary sites on top of this count.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has I said, we're going to move to a videotape marked Prosecution Exhibit 13.12. We'd ask that this videotape be played with sound, as it is Mr. Ruez himself who narrates this particular film.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So here is the Grbavci school with a playground, the gym and the main building. Going towards the top of the picture will be the direction to the execution site, and at the left you can see the railroad that is parallel to this asphalt road. Now, the helicopter is going to fly towards the execution site, and we'll give distance. Here at the middle is the dirt road going towards the underpass and to the first execution site. THE SPEAKER: On the 4th of April, 1996.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sound off. So this is the view from the railroad towards the second site, which is Lazete I, and this is the first execution site labelled "Lazete II." And here is the meadow that the witnesses say were ultimately covered with dead bodies. Here is a scene where Dr. Bill Haglund, who was together with us on that first mission there, is uncovering a piece of evidence which is a jacket, and there are human bones inside. Unfortunately, the -- the colour of the terrain doesn't enable to see exactly what Dr. Haglund is doing at this moment, but there are human bones inside a jacket. This is the area where the dump site is, and here various items that were found. These are socks. Other pieces of clothing, hats, caps, personal documents but with no names in it. It was mainly cover pages of ID cards in bad shape, and assorted personal items. Here is filming a knot on a piece of cloth, shoes. And here in total I think we found 117 pieces of cloth. MS. DE LA TORRE:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, leaving the site at Orahovac and the Grbavci school, we'll move to another school in the area known as the Petkovci school. MS. DE LA TORRE: And for the record and for the Defence, the witnesses who survived the killing at the Petkovci school and the nearby dam are Witness 67, P111; and Witness 68, P112.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, looking at Prosecution Exhibit 14.1, there is an aerial image of a building that you've labelled as "Petkovci." Could you explain to the Court what that particular building represents?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the so-called Petkovci school, which is in fact the new school of Petkovci. There is another school a bit further up the road at the left of the picture, a few hundred metres away, which is the old school, and that is the headquarters of one of the Zvornik Brigades at that time -- forward command post, sorry. This is the -- the school where two survivors declare having been kept prisoners. They were driven from Bratunac town on 14 July and were transported to -- to that school that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Court how --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said -- yes. What date did I say? 14 July. Yes, indeed. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Court how you first identified the Petkovci school as the location where these two individuals were detained.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the -- the only school in the vicinity of the dam, and we knew that the detention site was also close to the dam, since the survivors declared having driven a short distance from their last detention site to the execution site. So we went there, took photographs, and presented these photographs to the witnesses, who confirmed that this was indeed the school where they had been detained prior being transported to the dam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 14.2. Were there particular features of this school that enabled you to corroborate the witness accounts of having been held there?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a view of the entrance of the school from the back of the school where the -- the yard is, and the -- the witness describes his arrival at the school when getting out of the vehicle that transported him there, he had to walk down stairs in between a row of soldiers who were beating them. And once arriving inside the school, there was a very specific staircase that was going up to the first floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 14.3. Were the witnesses able to confirm using photographs such as this one of that staircase that this was in fact the school in which they had been held?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he precisely recognised this staircase, indeed. And he was held in one of the classrooms of the first floor. The two -- the two prisoners who survived were both on the first floor in separate classrooms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the survivors of this particular execution indicate where they had been shipped from prior to arriving at the Petkovci school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both of them were -- had spent the previous night in Bratunac in a vehicle lined in a convoy in a fixed position in one of the streets of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 14.4.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I'll just correct slightly the previous information. Because among all the survivors who ended up in the area north, one did spend a night in the -- on a vehicle that was in a convoy at the entrance of Kravica town -- village, and I don't know who this one is. All the others were coming from Bratunac town, but one convoy was in Kravica village and left also Kravica village the same morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 14.4. Could you explain to the Court what this is a picture of.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a picture of the corridor at the first floor of the school that leads to the classrooms, and these classrooms are located at the right hand of this corridor. One of the survivors believes he was in the last classroom at the right hand of this corridor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 14.5. There is a photograph of a dam. Could you explain the significance of this dam with regard to the school at Petkovci?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This dam is located approximately 3 -- 3 kilometres by the road from the Petkovci school. It is a dam which is in fact pumping waste from the aluminium factory of Karakaj. So you have a lake of red water, and then a very large wall, which is the dam itself, and at the bottom is a large plateau which has been used to -- as an execution field -- part of it as an execution field, to kill the prisoners who were taken there by -- by truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is the dam from the Petkovci school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just said I think it's approximately 3 kilometres from the school, by road. By air distance, it would be much closer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were the prisoners taken from the Petkovci school to the dam?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On July 14, once the school was full, the prisoners were taken out of this school. They were not blindfolded. They didn't have also their hands attached in their back. They were taken directly to this -- to this rocky plateau at the bottom of a dam, where they were instructed to get off of the vehicles and an execution squad was there waiting for them. They were requested to line up among the dead bodies, and they were then shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how long did the executions last at the dam site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the entire afternoon of the 14 and it continued during the evening, according to the two survivors who were on the spot and who were waiting to find a relevant moment to try to escape from this location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I just can't be quiet any longer. I'm sorry. But I just want to make clear on the record that we object to his whole line of testimony, from Mr. Jokic, because he continues to summarise. He's an OTP investigator. And he keeps testifying from facts that are not in evidence. Everything he keeps testifying to is not evidence before this court. It's more like an opening statement, because we've not seen any facts. All we have is summary from an OTP investigator. So our objection is please prevent the witness from testifying to facts not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the purpose of the testimony of this witness is to give us an overall picture of what happened at that time. So take the statements of the survivors, the witnesses, as a clue for his -- for the investigation. And he himself has been to that place and made some investigations. In this sense, his testimony has some probative value in it. Of course we'll hear other witnesses to testify to specific incidents that happened. As Ms. De la Torre indicated, there are two survivors during this incident and we are going to hear them to corroborate the testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Well, I would hope that this Trial Chamber would listen to the testimony of the survivors and not the OTP witness who is testifying at the minute who is summarising basically the opening statement of the Prosecutor. As an example, counsel has been to those sites too, but I'm not allowed to summarise what I think the testimony will be from some witness we might call. I just think it's unacceptable that he's able to say, "This is what happened. This is what happened next," and it's -- he's testifying to facts that are not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But anyway, in the future we'll hear the live testimony of those, you know, two survivors later on, and to see whether it's corroborated with this witness's testimony or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: As long as the Court accepts the -- the best evidence rule as the best evidence in this Trial Chamber. I'm sure you will. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will bear that in mind. You may sit down please. You may proceed, Ms. De la Torre. MS. DE LA TORRE: Did you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 14.7, Mr. Ruez, were there elements on the scene that you were able -- I'm sorry -- yeah, looking at Prosecution Exhibit 14.6, first of all, you've indicated the approximate size of the execution area. Could you explain to the Court how you were able to determine the approximate length and width of the killing field there at the dam.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the course of the missions that were conducted on the plateau of this dam, items were collected on the surface and they were mapped by -- by the forensic archaeologist who was doing then later on the exhumation here. And I think this map is part of his report, and this report is introduced here. All the shell casings that were found on this terrain were mapped, as well as also a number -- a large number of skull fragments that were found in this area. We later on also came back with the survivors on this crime scene and they showed on the ground the size of that terrain that was covered with bodies when they could observe this -- this location. These two witnesses escaped together from this site, and they crawled towards the hill that you can see just in front, where it is written "approximate size of the execution area," is the place where they were hiding then during the night and the next morning and from where they could observe the spot. And this -- the yellow -- the area marked in yellow roughly covers the area where the items were discovered, as well as the area that the victims pinpointed as being an area of the plateau where the bodies were lying on. In fact, I on purpose made this area smaller on this photograph than what it is actually on the map of Mr. -- of Professor Wright. I prefer to be -- to minimise the size of -- of a scene than to -- having enlarge it of a few centimetres on the picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 14.7. Were you able to corroborate the witness accounts of their escape from that particular execution using the elements depicted in this particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They describe having crawled along -- I mean, along the bottom of this plateau, and they then entered a concrete ditch that was separating the dam from the forest area. And this is a photograph of the ditch that is running from -- at the top of the picture guardhouse to the bottom of the dam, and this is the area that they in fact crossed before reaching the forest. I would also add one element, which is that at the top right of the picture, just where the number 57 is, is a pylon with a ramp of lamps. And the witnesses claim that during that night when the execution was going on in the evening, these -- this ramp of lamps was lit so that the killers could continue to work on the scene.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned previously that the witnesses stayed in the area and were able to observe the murders take place as well as the subsequent burial process. Were you able to corroborate that the place from which the witnesses claimed to have seen the murders as well as the clean-up was in fact a place in which you could observe those events?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- the following day, when they were on this -- on this hill, in fact they started crawling towards the east in order to find an escape route. And during that day, they didn't hear but they heard single shots, which were for them consistent with the fact that the wounded were being killed during that day of the 15th, since they could -- they could observe that it was not the fact the day before, all the wounded were not killed the day before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to the location from which they claimed to have been able to observe the events below them after the murders ceased?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that they claimed having seen the things. They remembered having heard single shots during that day, and they arrived at the conclusion that it was finishing the wounded process.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But moving on to the -- to the subsequent clean-up process, did they observe the clean-up as it transpired the following day?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The next day they noticed that there was a front loader on this plateau. It was -- that vehicle was -- that machine was already there the previous day. And there was also a tractor with a trailer, and the front loader was loading the trailer with bodies. These -- the tractor then left the scene and drove up to the dam, and then they lost it from sight but they noticed a rotation that was lasting approximately 20 minutes. So during the day of the 15th, obviously bodies were taken away from that scene and taken to an unknown direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 14.8.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may interrupt for one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Before we move, there was a question posed to the witness I believe two or three times whether he went to the location where these witnesses saw what they allegedly claim they saw and will testify to, and we never got an answer from the witness. Perhaps we could get an answer from the witness. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. De la Torre, would you please re-ask your question so that we could hear what the witness is going to answer to that question. MS. DE LA TORRE:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, did you go to the location from which these witnesses claimed to have been able to see the burial process and confirm whether or not you could in fact see the events they claimed to have witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I went to the -- on the hill where they said that they stayed, but they -- the only thing they claimed that they have seen from there is the transporting -- the loading of the bodies on the trailer. They do not claim having seen where this vehicle went, because indeed from where they were they could not see that. It's impossible. Once the tractor is taking the -- the road going up -- uphill, which is on this photograph marked with the yellow line, at one point you lose the vehicle in sight. And indeed they could not see then later on what was happening. They could only see indeed the vehicle coming back empty, but they could not pinpoint what was happening with the -- the load of that trailer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a matter of fact, without interruption, that is where I was going to go. You mentioned that they at some point couldn't see the truck. Were you able to verify that the point from which they claimed to have been witnessing the events, it was in fact true that there was a point in time in which you cannot observe the truck?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to -- to this point in their story, have you been able to corroborate every -- each of the events as they claimed them to have occurred to this point, the fact that they escaped via a canal?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, we didn't pinpoint any -- any impossibility on the ground that would enable one to say that they saw something that they couldn't see physically. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to verify that there was indeed a guardhouse, as they claimed?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to indeed verify the fact that there were lights that they claimed illuminated the murders as they occurred?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never checked if these lights were still in function when we went there, but the pylon with the lamps on it was still there, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to verify that there was indeed a hill from which you could look down upon the site with the bodies?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to verify the fact that from that particular position there is a point in time at which you cannot -- you lose sight of a truck headed towards the peninsula?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking of the peninsula, in Prosecution Exhibit 14.8 you have marked -- or there is depicted a peninsula in a body of water that is orange. You've marked a box around the end of that peninsula. Could you explain to the Court what that particular box represents?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This represents what we call the peninsula, which is an area that enters the lake. The importance of it is that we tried to find a location in the vicinity of the dam where the bodies might have been buried. We tried that by using aerial imagery and that led to no results, so the assumption we made was that it was maybe possible that these bodies had been dumped into the water. Unfortunately, we would not be able to give a final answer to this for the reason that though the entire area, which is in the yellow marked box, has been probed by the team of Professor Richard Wright, one part of it could not be dealt with because of a presence of unknown chemicals. So the -- the location where these bodies have been taken to is, as far as we are concerned, still a mystery. But it has to be taken in account once we will make a final count of minimum number of -- of individuals, once we will have connected the secondary sites where the bodies have been relocated, the number will have to be added to the number of bodies that have been found inside the mass grave located on the plateau. But this will not, unfortunately, give the final figure of how many people have been killed there because of this disappearance of bodies that were transported during the 15th and which we could not locate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to explore the water itself in order to determine whether or not there were any bodies dumped in the water?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it was much too late after these events. And as I said, the water here is -- is a waste pumped from the aluminium factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that why it's orange on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 14.9. Were you, however, able to confirm using aerial imagery that there was in fact a disturbance at that site that corroborated the testimony of the witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see on these two photographs, one at the left dated 5 July 1995, that -- how the plateau looks like seen from above and compared with an aerial photograph dated 27 July 1995. There is an area of disturbance that happens -- that appears on the photograph. In fact, the only one that has to be considered here is the one that is on the plateau. The little arrow pointing to the intersection of a dirt road, the area was probed, and as far as I know nothing was found there. But when we started probing the disturbed area which is visible on the picture, we found a piece of human skull 1 metre deep under the rocks, and this sparked the need of doing an exhumation on this site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Taking into consideration the area that's marked in brackets that you referred to, can you explain to the Court and now turning to Prosecution Exhibit 14.10, is this the skull that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the -- the piece of human skull that we found when we dug in this rocky plateau.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
