utterances.text: Could you explain to the Court what else was found during the course of the exhumation of that particular site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a site that also has been disturbed later, end of September, beginning of October, but there were human bones found in the initial primary mass grave, and I think the number -- the minimum number of individuals represented by this bone collection was around 50 persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And without going into the details, Mr. Ruez, during the course of your investigation, was the site at Petkovci and the murders that occurred there ultimately linked to a secondary grave site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The secondary grave sites connected with this primary site are located in the area of Lipovi, and all the elements that connect these sites be detailed by Dean Manning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking now at another school in the immediate vicinity, the school at Rocevic. Could you explain to the Court, using Prosecution Exhibit 15.1, how it was that you first identified the Rocevic school as a potential crime scene.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a photograph of the school of Rocevic, when seen from the road that goes from Zvornik to -- towards Bijeljina. It is on top of a hill. It is not directly from the asphalt road. I would think it was a zoom in on the picture that is on the hill. In fact, we didn't have any -- we didn't have during long any indication that prisoners were kept inside this school before 1999, when we got confirmation of that from some Serb personnel that we interviewed in 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm going to have to object to non-responsive from the witness because the Prosecutor asked him how was it that you first identified the Rocevic school as a potential crime scene. And then the witness started going into his own narrative about what he wanted to tell the Court instead of answering the Prosecutor's question. Could you ask the witness to please be more responsive to the questions of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the witness has not come to that point yet. Probably he will. Let's wait and see, you know, how he's going to answer that question. MS. DE LA TORRE:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, perhaps I misheard you, but I thought I heard you indicate that in interviews with Serb witnesses this particular site was identified as a holding site for prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object. I believe the Prosecutor is testifying now for the witness, instead of asking him questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe it's a wrong characterisation of what the witness said. MS. DE LA TORRE:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, could you repeat what you said previously with regard to the Serb interviews you conducted and their relation to the identification of the Rocevic school as a holding facility for prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, initially we had no information at all regarding the use that was done of that school during the events. When we were driving in the area, we always were astonished, never having come across any information regarding this school, since it is sandwiched in between the area north, which is Pilica, and the area south, which is the sites of Orahovac and the dam we just talked about, so we were wondering about this. But we never went there because we never had any survivor who talked about that school and we never had any information telling us that this school had been used, and this was the case until 1999. It's only in 1999 that we got confirmation of a document that had been seized at the Zvornik Brigade and that was the record of a vehicle log indicating various locations in this area that had been visited by this vehicle. All areas we know about, Orahovac, the dam, Pilica. The only location we didn't know about and that was mentioned on this log was Rocevic. It is only later through interview processes that some people - and I don't know if they will or not come to testify about this - confirmed that indeed that school has been used as a detention site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, is the school at Rocevic in close proximity to an execution site that was uncovered subsequently at Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 16.1. Could you describe to the Court the proximity of Rocevic to the execution site at Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The school of Rocevic is approximately 3 kilometres far from Kozluk, taking the asphalt road -- the natural road that goes to Kozluk. And once in Kozluk, there is a turn to the left that leads to a dirt road that is running close to the Drina River, and at the end of that dirt road, approximately 2 kilometres far from Kozluk, is an area of a gravel pit just at the -- just next to the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Court how it was in the course of the investigation that you first identified Kozluk as an execution site.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So here the -- the chain of events that led us to this site is a bit -- a pit more complex, since there are no survivors -- no known survivors for this Kozluk execution site. The information initially was a rumour, a rumour among refugees who were in a refugee centre in Germany and who were still in contact with local Serbs in Kozluk. One of these refugees was interviewed by a colleague named Jan Kruszweski who told him what the rumour as about and drew a sketch of the area of Kozluk. To summarise the rumour, it is that approximately that 500 people had been killed in the area of the gravel pits of Kozluk close to a specific pit named the Ferida pit. Based with this hearsay information, we requested aerial imagery of that spot of gravel pits, and the aerial imagery confirmed that there was a disturbance there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 16.2, there is indeed an aerial image on the left dated 5 July 1995 and on the right 17 July 1995. Does this particular area correspond to the information that was obtained from the refugee?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the area that matches the -- the sketch that was done by this -- this indirect witness and led us to the be interested on this site. At the left of the picture the grey area is the Drina River. And just at the edge of it is this dirt road. On July 5 one can see at the left -- in fact, the -- the pit of gravel, but at the right now one can see that there has been a large -- a large disturbance in that zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 16.3. There is a colour photograph of this site. Does this photograph depict the killing field as it stands there by the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a -- this is a photograph. The river is at the back, and in front is the -- the area where the execution apparently took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you mentioned earlier that there were no survivors from the execution that occurred in Kozluk. Based upon that, are you able to determine how many people were murdered here?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time we went on -- I'll answer yes. To explain that, I would have to -- to say that one day in 1998, as we were together with Richard Wright during the exhumation of a secondary site that we code named Cancari III, during this exhumation suddenly was uncovered quite a large quantity of piled glass, green -- green glass, broken bottles, and when -- after that discovery was also uncovered from the exhumation site a stack of labels on which one could read Vitinka factory Kozluk. At that time we had not yet done any -- any observations on the Kozluk site, so we decided to do that as soon as possible and went there the following day. We passed by this Vitinka factory, which is in fact a building next to the headquarters of the Drina Wolves, which is a unit attached to the Zvornik Brigade, and that is at the entrance of this dirt path that leads to -- to the site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just stop you there, Mr. Ruez. You indicated that in the grave there were fragments of green glass and Vitinka bottling labels. Were you able to determine whether or not the Vitinka bottling factory in Kozluk did indeed use green bottle glass?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Since I went on the spot in this location we found stacks of broken glass, which is probably the area where this factory deposits the broken -- the broken glass, and also stacks of labels which were the same ones that were found in Cancari III.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Among other things, did that discovery there in Kozluk of the bottles and the labels connect the site of the murders at Kozluk with the exhumation that was being conducted at Cancari?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among other things, indeed it does. And this is what enables us then to answer your initial question which is connected with the number of bodies. Because this site, although it was disturbed and the bodies relocated, still contained -- still contained 340 bodies that had been left on the spot after the disturbance process. And in the secondary site of Cancari road III, 158 persons were exhumed from this site. So that is a total of 506 bodies for this crime scene, and that is a number that matches the -- the initial rumour that -- that we heard about. It's still -- it is still not yet certain that there are no more mass graves connected with this site, so this number could only inflate maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned that in addition to the Vitinka bottling factory in the area there were -- there was the Drina Wolves headquarters. Could you explain to the Court how far approximately it is from the murder scene at Kozluk to the Drina Wolves headquarters?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately more than 1 kilometre, knowing that one has to pass in front of this military facility to go to that spot and one has to pass in front of it to leave this spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it's more or less a dead-end area here. It's an area of cornfields.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 16.4. This is an aerial image. Does this assist you in demonstrating to the Court the distance between the Drina Wolves headquarters and the execution site there at Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The aim of this exhibit is to show the landscape, the fact that it's a remote area close to the river. It shows Kozluk at the -- at the distance. Kozluk here is 2 to 3 kilometres away. And where the -- the yellow square is top right there is one building which I believe is the Vitinka factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll now turn to Prosecution Exhibit 16.5, which is a video taken of the scene at Kozluk. Mr. Ruez, were you present when this particular videotape was taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This one, I filmed. MS. DE LA TORRE: If we could play that now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So here -- here is the Drina River. In front of us is the -- is the site. Then there is the -- the dirt road here. Then Kozluk, white building in the middle, the Vitinka factory, and the -- here the helicopter turns to show the area around that site in between the asphalt and the river, which is only a large area of cornfields without many houses. This is a view from the ground, the river, looking towards Kozluk, the access path, the area of disturbance. And here it makes a turn. This is broken glass. Here is a piece of human remains. This is a slope of disturbed soil with one shoe with a foot inside. This is another shoe. This is another pile of broken glass. Shell casings embedded in the ground on -- on the dirt path that is just at the edge of the area where the grave is and the execution site was. All these shell casings around the grave or in the grave were also later on used to make comparisons with shell casings that were found in the secondary site that is connected with it. Pieces of clothing. Again, shell casing. The same, human remains as previously. Again, the same shoe with the foot inside. Shell casings mixed with broken glass on disturbed soil. Hard to see here, human vertebra. Very clear traces of -- of disturbance here, human bone. Some human remains were sticking out of the ground, and when we started to see how deep it would go we realised that in fact we would be starting -- starting an exhumation if we would continue this. Here it shows in the vicinity large piles of broken glass. This is a stack of items among which are also labels of Vitinka factory, and this -- this trash area is in fact a former Muslim cemetery. This is a gravestone which was found there. And here are labelled exactly of the same type than those that were found during the exhumation of a secondary site. This is a view of when exiting the area, returning to Kozluk, this is the -- the building where the Drina Wolves are billeting, and the Vitinka factory next to it. This is the entrance to the unit, and next to it is the factory that produces the broken glass and the labels. And this is the patch of the unit. This is the -- going straight here is the direction of the -- of a site, and this is the -- the junction with the asphalt road in Kozluk town. This is a scene of the same site, but during the exhumation process. It's the same area that was shown previously, but here in its full size. Here is an area where the bodies are getting uncovered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. De la Torre, it is time for a break. MS. DE LA TORRE: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And at this stage, can you indicate to us how much time do you still need to conduct the direct examination. MS. DE LA TORRE: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. MS. DE LA TORRE: I'm sorry. I would say, Your Honour, approximately an hour to an hour and a half we have remaining for Mr. Ruez. We do have three -- I'm sorry, two more videos which are total 11 minutes, and three more crime scenes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. MS. DE LA TORRE: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, prior to the break, you mentioned an aspect of your investigation that I believe bears some explanation, and that's with regard to shell casings. In the course of your investigation, did you attempt to match shell casings from the various crime scenes?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And without going into all of the expert particulars, can you give the Judges an overview of whether or not you were able to identify shell casings to different crime scenes and shell casings from -- or to the weapons from which they were fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't believe the witness has been qualified as an expert on -- on ballistics. If the question is: Was it tested and is he aware of the results? I don't have a problem. But if he's going to be testifying as an expert, I do have a problem unless he's qualified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't think this witness will testify as an expert witness. But what -- we'll hear what he's going to tell us on this specific aspect. MS. DE LA TORRE:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I said, Mr. Ruez, if you could just give us an overview of whether or not as a part of your investigation you attempted to determine whether or not crime scenes matched from various locations as well as whether or not shell casings were matched between the crime scenes and any weapon from which it might have been fired.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The aim of the process of collecting shell casings was to match sites each with another. We have to separate that in three groups. One group would be the shell casings found on a suspected execution site. These are shell casings where used to be compared with the shell casings which were found inside the mass grave associated with this execution site. And then the third group of shell casings are the shell casings that are found inside the so-called secondary mass graves, the goal being to ascertain that the shell casings of the executions -- of the execution site, once compared with the primary mass grave, we find indeed the same type of -- of traces -- I mean, how to explain this? Without entering in any kind of an expertise, the way it's compared is the extraction mark of -- that leaves -- that is left on the shell casings by the extractor of the weapon, and this leaves a specific mark, that identifies one weapon. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do have to object because I have maybe a little more expertise in ballistics, and you have to have the weapon in order to do the rifling in the barrel to test where the casings came from. So unless you know -- have the weapon to test it, they can't verify who fired the weapon or where the casing came from or any kind of sign from that weapon. So I don't believe that he can testify about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Sinatra, I think this witness is just to tell us what he did when he found those -- those casings, which is not expert testimony and which is not required by the Prosecution from this witness. This witness is going to tell us the fact that he found those casings and make a comparison of those casings. It may be right; it may be wrong. We may proceed. MS. DE LA TORRE:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, as you indicated, did you collect shell casings from execution sites and attempt to match them to grave sites?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you take shell casings from primary grave sites and attempt to match them to secondary grave sites?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the course of your investigation, was there ever an attempt made to match shell casings to any particular weapon or weapons?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the second phase, that was an attempt that we made. And though we seized a large number of weapons and test-fired these weapons, we did not have any positive match between the shell casings and the weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that particular aspect of the investigation was unsuccessful.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving from the murders that were committed at Kozluk to the Pilica school -- MS. DE LA TORRE: For the record, the Pilica school survivors -- Pilica school and/or Branjevo Farm survivors are Witness 69, P105; Witness 70, P113; and Witness 71, P116.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 17.1, Mr. Ruez, could you explain to the Court what this particular photograph represents.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph is an aerial view of Pilica school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain where the Pilica school is in relation to a location you later identified as the Branjevo Farm?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When going north, Zvornik, in the direction of Bijeljina, there is a village named Pilica that is along the asphalt road that leads -- so from Zvornik to Bijeljina. And from there there is a gravel road that leads approximately after 3 kilometres to a large building which is this Pilica school, composed of one two-storey building and one gymnasium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was it, Mr. Ruez, that you were first able to identify the Pilica school as a holding site for prisoners?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in possession of the interviews of three persons who claimed having survived an execution nearby that place and having been detained in that school prior to that execution. They made a description of -- of a building, and I don't remember exactly how we ended up pinpointing this school. I think it was with the assistance of police personnel in Tuzla who -- who found out that there was a large school in the vicinity of Pilica, and then we went to -- to identify this place, photograph it, and present the material to the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you presented the photographs to the survivors of this particular execution, were they able to identify that as the school -- the Pilica school as the location where they had been held?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to ascertain how many prisoners were detained at the Pilica school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We have the knowledge that the gymnasium was full of prisoners, and this would have to be checked with the survivors, but as far as I recall one of them was also held in the -- in the classrooms. So apparently the entire structure was used to keep prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the prisoners first begin to arrive at the Pilica school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On July 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they coming from?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least for one of them, coming from the so-called old school in Bratunac, which was apparently the last building in Bratunac town, emptied of its prisoners 15th July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Referring to the Exhibit 17.1, you have marked what is labelled a "water pump" as well as an "execution site." Given the information that you obtained from the witnesses who survived being held here, can you explain to the Court the significance of both the water pump and the execution site.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is to highlight one part of the testimony of one of these witnesses, who claims that at one point when he was inside the gym he was tasked to fetch some water in order to provide water to his fellow prisoners. So he exited the gymnasium and went to an area that he called the water pump area, that indeed we easily found in the vicinity of that school, and that is marked -- the location is marked on the photograph with the yellow box. And we presented him also more close shots of this water pump, pump. These exhibits are not -- are not here. And he recognised all these locations and explained that when he was coming back from this water pump, he could witness that one bus just was arriving in that location, that the people were requested to go out of these buses, and he saw them being grouped in what initially he called a meadow, and a circle of soldiers formed and they shot this group of prisoners in front of the school. When we brought this witness on the spot, he pinpointed a specific location as being that spot, and this is the location where it is in fact just where "school" is written on the photograph. One can see a little group of trees. This is the location he designated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Referring first to the water pump. When you yourself went to this scene and located the water pump, did it in fact correspond to the account that had been given to you by the witness, in terms of size, location, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the pump was matching his description. Indeed, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to the execution that the witness claimed to have witnessed, were you able to locate an area that corresponded to the location which the witness claimed had been used as an execution site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I will just correct one thing. In calling this a water pump, it's not a water pump. It's a pipe. It's a pipe, and water just flows out of this pipe. As far as the execution site described by this witness, the only elements that could be found and could be used to implement what he was saying was shell casings embedded in the ground, not in the area where the people were supposed having been killed but in the vicinity of it. We have marked photographs which we don't show here today and who -- who show where we did find these shell casings, and there were also traces on the wall that were matching directions of fire and indicating that indeed at this location some shooting might have occurred, since traces were visible on the -- on the facade of this building and that some of these traces had already been filled with concrete, probably the year before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were the prisoners who were detained at the Pilica school on the 15th of July taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 16th in the morning, according to the declarations of these witnesses, they were taken out of the school, told they would be going for exchange. At least one of them was blindfolded. They were taken onboard of a bus and driven towards the -- the asphalt road, which is the normal way they would have taken if they had indeed been going for an exchange. But then the bus turned right, continued on the gravel road, and led the prisoners to the Branjevo Farm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 18.1, there is an aerial overview of the location identified as the -- identified as Branjevo Farm. MS. DE LA TORRE: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you actually been to this location, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe for the Court how it was that you located this location as the site to which the prisoners from Pilica school were taken.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In March 1996, Drazen Erdemovic was arrested in Belgrade. And based on the first information that came out regarding what he was saying about the events in that location on 16 July, we requested aerial imagery of this place, and it is thanks to this imagery that we could orient ourselves and reach that farm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is Drazen Erdemovic?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drazen Erdemovic is a member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment who participated in the killings that occurred that day at the Branjevo Farm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the record, Your Honour, Drazen Erdemovic is a witness on the Prosecution witness list. Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 18.2, there is a panorama -- a colour panorama of the site from the ground. Could you point to the key elements on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the entrance of the farm, and the path that leads to the farm is the location where the buses were stopping. Erdemovic later on explained us in detail based on these photographs where what the process was. In fact, this is more or less the view that one would have when looking out of the window of a bus. At the right hand where the -- in the direction of where the helicopter is standing and where people can be seen at the distance, this is the area of the execution site. The prisoners were walked towards these buildings, then turned right towards the garage at the middle right of the picture. There is a tree next to it that some victims -- well, at least one victim referred to. And behind this garage was the execution squad that was waiting for the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 18.3. You've marked on this photograph a red arrow. What does that red arrow represent?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a view of the same garage or shed but at another date, and now there is a little fence in front. The same tree I pinpointed previously. So the people had to walk at the right hand of this structure towards this field, and the arrow marks in fact the location of the execution field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on to Prosecution Exhibit 18.4. There is an aerial image on which you've marked the approximate size of the execution area. Could you explain to the Court how it was that you were able to make the determination depicted here of the length and the width of the killing field at Branjevo Farm.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Three elements enable us, I believe, to assess the area of the execution field. One is the description that Drazen Erdemovic made of the process of the execution, first lining up the people, then shooting at them, then having another group arriving, passing that line, lining them up again, and like this advancing and advancing on this meadow. When we went there, we made also a collection process of shell casings at the surface of this field, and we marked the location where we were finding shell casings with yellow markers, and we ended up finding surface shell casings on an area which is approximately of the size of what I have marked on this photograph. In fact, we found shell casings in -- even further than this, but one has to know that in between the time the execution happened and the moment we went to collect shell casings, the field had been plundered, so machines have turned the soil upside down and some shell casings may have been transported further away?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we found shell casings at a greater distance than that, but they were -- they might have been taken during that process.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the minimum size, I mean. It's not the maximum size. It's the minimum size. And the third element is aerial imagery that shows bodies on the ground in this area as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 18.5, is this in fact an aerial image of the site that was utilised to determine the size of the killing field?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you explain to the Court what this image depicts.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is an aerial image dated 17 July, showing the -- the Branjevo Farm. At the top is the little dirt road that then will connect with the asphalt road at the level of Pilica village. So this is an area hidden from the asphalt road. From the asphalt road no one can see what is happening at this -- in this farm. One can see the line going from the top to the buildings. That is the path we showed previously, where the buses were unloading the prisoners and then were making a U-turn at the farm. The garage is also visible on this picture, and then there is the open field, where one group of bodies is lying on the ground and also many traces of vehicles, which in fact are the traces of the front loader who probably went to collect these -- the bodies. The traces on the picture are not traces of a bus or -- or any other type of vehicle. It was at this point on this photo, in fact, collecting bodies where the area is marked "bodies," and in order to dump them in a mass grave that is located bottom left of the picture, where again two markings of bodies are made on the photograph, one in fact being bodies that are already in the grave and one in a stack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the aerial image labelled Prosecution Exhibit 18.4 corroborate both the survivor testimony as well as that of Drazen Erdemovic?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 18. -- sorry, that was 18.5. Okay. Looking at 18.6, excuse me, there is a photograph dated 21 September 1995. Could you explain the significance of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So on this photograph -- that photograph shows the same thing as the previous one, but from another angle here again. Here again we can see at the top of the picture the dirt road going towards Pilica on the left and Zvornik to the right. In fact, the asphalt road is much further up this picture, not visible on the same photo. And comparing this photo with the previous one, one can still see 21 September 1995 the traces -- the white traces that mark the terrain that has been disturbed when the bodies were removed from the execution site and now shows the precise location of the burial area where the mass grave was initially located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 18.7. Between the survivor testimony, the testimony of Drazen Erdemovic, and the evidence collected during the course of the exhumations, were you able to ascertain approximately how many people were murdered at Branjevo Farm?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, for various reasons. One -- the first reason being that since the primary mass grave has been disturbed, until we won't have finalised the exhumation of all the secondary mass graves which can be connected with this site, no minimum -- total minimum number of individuals will be provided. In this mass grave -- disturbed mass grave, the number of bodies that was found during the exhumation in 1996 is 132, minimum number of individuals. Secondary sites connected with this primary site have been located in a valley named Cancari, where several mass graves are connected with this one. Until final exhumation, no number can be presented. And the other problem with numbers here will be that the next crime scene we will be talking about, which is the Pilica house of culture, we have reasons to believe that the bodies were also buried at the Branjevo Farm. So we have two -- two execution sites and one burial site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Drazen Erdemovic able to give an estimate of the number of people that were shot during his time as an executioner at Branjevo Farm?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He -- he declared that between 10.00 in the morning and, I think, 3.00 p.m. they shot about -- more than 1.000 people on this field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Ruez, is that inconsistent with the witness survivor reports of how many bodies that they saw on the meadow when they were taken for their execution?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that it is not inconsistent with the capacity of Pilica school. I don't recall that the victims here made any assessment of numbers when they were talking about what they could see on the execution field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on to Prosecution Exhibit 18.8. There is a video. It's approximately four minutes long, of this scene as Branjevo Farm. Were you present when this video was made, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. MS. DE LA TORRE: If we could play that video now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the -- this is the field. Here it is a zoom-in on the area where the grave was created. And here we can see the farm and the access to the farm. At the distance is the -- the highway that goes from Zvornik towards Pilica. So this is again filmed by Peter Nicholson, sound off. This is the -- the field where the people were standing at the left was the in brackets, the rest area for the 10th Sabotage Detachment people. Where the trees are at the left; one has to turn left to access where the grave is. And all this in front is the execution meadow. This is the little garage and the tree. And here we had lined up and walked all along this field in order to mark with yellow stickers the locations where we were seeing shell casings. We didn't use metal detectors. We were only taking into account those we could see on the surface that day. So here we are still finding casings. In the distance one can still see -- one can see the garage. And the grave would be at the right hand of this picture, in that direction here. Some shell casings were found further in that direction, but that is away from the -- from the execution area, too far away. This is probably a casing that has been moved there at the moment this field was cultivated. MS. DE LA TORRE:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. MS. DE LA TORRE:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, we were previously discussing a detention site known as the Pilica school. And you recently made reference to another location which you referred to as the Pilica Dom. Could you explain to the Court what the Pilica Dom is.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Pilica Dom, we call it the Dom, that is house of culture, the culture house of the village of Pilica. It is the municipal building used for festivities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is the Pilica Dom from the Branjevo Farm?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not more than 2 to 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 19.1, there is an aerial image with -- which is marked "House of culture and cafe." Can you explain to the Court the significance of the cafe and its proximity to the Pilica Dom or the house of culture?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I will have to refer to the testimonies of Drazen Erdemovic. Erdemovic says that once the execution was completed at the Branjevo Farm, the lieutenant colonel came and instructed both those of the 10th Sabotage Detachment but as well elements that were with them and who, according to Erdemovic, were coming to from Bratunac. That entire group was instructed to go to the house of culture where allegedly a group of 500 prisoners were attempting to break out from. The members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, according to Erdemovic, refused to commit this execution, claiming they had done enough for that day. And the other volunteer group to do it. So they all went to Pilica. And meanwhile, those who came from Bratunac committed the killings at the house of culture, Erdemovic was sitting in a cafe that he said was just in front of that building, and this is the cafe that is marked on this photograph and that is at the opposite side of -- of the road in front of the house of culture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to corroborate that there is indeed a cafe, as you mentioned, across from the house of culture that Drazen Erdemovic said it was?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. And from that cafe, one -- one cannot see, because of another little building in between, the entrance of this house of culture but indeed could see, as Erdemovic claimed, events that happened outside it when people managed to run out and were shot in the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 19.2, there is a closer view of this particular location.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So on this one, one can clearly see how the -- how the buildings are located in relation each to another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, during the course of your investigation, is there anything about the Pilica Dom as an execution site that is unusual with regard to its location?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All the other locations in the area we called the area north are in remote places, both detention sites and the execution sites. They are all at a distance of the main road, let's say, even though they are in inhabited areas like Grbavci, for example. This is the only location where people have been detained just prior execution in an area that was populated and where a lot of witnesses around could observe what is happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on to Prosecution Exhibit 19.3. Could you explain to the Court when you were first able to visit the Pilica Dom as part of your investigation.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was in 1996. June 1996 we -- we went first -- we tried to locate -- to locate the building that -- and we -- what we did, we ended up finding -- finding this building alongside of the road and visited it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking -- and before we go to Prosecution Exhibit 19.4, there is a close-up of a door. Could you indicate on 19.3 which door it was that you entered through for the first time?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You have here the -- at the front of the building, one can see that there is a door. That door leads in fact to -- to a part of a building that is no more connected with the -- the main room where the celebrations take place. The door that connects these places has been sealed in between the events and the moment we came. The door that leads to the -- to the main room is the door that is more to the right, a blue door, on the -- yes, this one. So this is the door to access the inside of -- of the main room, and there is door, but behind the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 19.4, as I mentioned, there is a close-up of this door with a lock on it. What is the significance of this photograph, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this photograph is upside down, but it doesn't make too much difference. The interest of it is that between the moment of the -- after the events here, we have indications that the area has been cleaned, cleaned of the bodies and other elements that could be found there, like shell casings. And after this process, somebody probably locked this door so that curious people would not enter it. And this is the shape in which we found the door when we first arrived in June 1996, with a lock and spider nests in between that seem to indicate that it's already a while ago that no one entered this place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving inside the Dom, Mr. Ruez, there's Prosecution Exhibit 19.6. Could you explain to the Court how this particular facility was used prior to the war.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I named the main room, which is the -- the room where the people had celebrations or maybe also movie theatre, since this picture is taken from a room that is apparently a projectionist's cabin with two holes that enabled them to project films in this location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I might have misspoke. This is Prosecution Exhibit 19.5. Looking at 19.6, there is a close-up of the area around the stairs. What is this a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. This is a close-up of the area of the stage, which is probably the area where the victims were being pushed at the moments fire was opened up on them, because there are possibilities to hide behind -- behind this wall. So these are obvious traces that were seen in this location when we entered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on to Exhibit 19.7. There is a photograph of the wall at the back of the building, at the back of the area you described as the theatre. Could you explain to the Court what in particular this photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph of the stage and the wall behind it, and indeed it is the area of the building which is the most damaged. All these traces have been sampled for analysis, and the reports are introduced showing that many of them are explosive residues and human residues. And also the stage is damaged, probably by explosion grenades which have damaged it and also left traces on the -- on the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 19.9. This is an aerial image dated 17 July 1995. On it you've marked the cafe and the Pilica Dom, the culture hall, as well as what you've identified as an unidentified vehicle. What is the significance of that particular vehicle vis-a-vis the Dom on 17 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have knowledge of that -- the bodies at the Branjevo Farm were being buried that day. One survivor of the Branjevo Farm massacre that day, the 17th, he is moving in the area and he sees one truck transporting dead bodies. We don't know exactly where he saw that truck moving dead bodies around, but the only location we know where bodies are at that -- at that day and cannot be buried on the spot is indeed the Pilica house of culture, so we made the assumption that the bodies were taken from the Pilica Dom were then taken to the Branjevo Farm and that cleaning process seemed to have happened the 17th July, because that is the day where this truck is spotted, but it's also the day where on this imagery there is one vehicle that is backing against the entrance door of the culture hall. And on another picture we will see also that another vehicle has left traces to go behind this building, where through another door one can also enter the location and remove what was inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just for clarification, that's Prosecution Exhibit 19.8. 19.9 is in fact a blow-up of this scene, albeit not great quality. You mentioned a moment ago that there were in fact two doors. Are those doors marked on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The marking that is on the top of the picture is the -- the main entrance that I -- that we showed previously, with this blue iron door. And at the back of the building is another -- is another way to access.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also marked the photograph with the words "tire tracks."

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain the significance of that marking.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These markings indicate that one vehicle also went to the back door of this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this point, Mr. Ruez, we have a video of the scene at the Pilica Dom labelled "Prosecution Exhibit 19.10." Were you present when this video was made?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. MS. DE LA TORRE: If we could play that now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So that's the sign that indicates that it is indeed the cultural house in Pilica. Here the camera is turning towards the cafe. This is the cafe, opposite side of the street. Here is the front entrance, only leads to a room, and at the left at that time was a little communication centre, telephone centre. Here was probably an access to the inside of the main -- the main room, but there has been a fresh sealing done on it. Someone - and it was not us - broke a little part of this sealed door, probably to have a look at the inside. This is what one could see through this little opening. This shows the area around with houses. This is a view from the cabin of a projectionist, the two openings that are used to project films. In that part of the building where the projectionist's cabin is, there were also shell casings on the ground, indicating that someone opened fire on the people inside from this opening. The place has been analysed by forensic experts, and the report has been introduced on this. So this is again the cabin of the projectionist, with a staircase going down. And here the example is one shell casing is pushed on the side by someone who broomed the place. This is the main access door. This is a plastic glove, and this is where the -- the truck was backed against -- an unidentified vehicle was backed against this door. Here is a shell casing, another shell casing. So this is now the main entrance open. The door at the left is the door that leads to the projectionist's cabin. This is the inside of the main room. Shell casings still to be found. It's part of the rough cleaning process that happened inside. This is a bullet; a shell casing. These are pieces of identification cards that were found on the spot, under the stage. Here is the ID of a person born in Srebrenica, and his name is on the missing list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, are there any known survivors from the massacre at the Pilica Dom?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No survivor that we know of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning your attention now to Prosecution Exhibit 20.1. You have created a map, Mr. Ruez, which outlines your testimony concerning the detention sites and the execution sites. We have Prosecution Exhibit 20.1A, which is a key to this map. Using this map, Mr. Ruez, that you've created, could you explain to the Court geographically the significance of these particular locations vis-a-vis one another and with regard to the distinction you made between the north and the south.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So here -- this is a map that reproduces -- that marks on the ground all the main crime scenes we -- we went to. If one could make a border between these two areas, it would be more or less at the junction of the asphalt road with the Drina River at the bottom -- at the middle -- middle right of this photograph -- of this map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using what you have marked with pink, I'm sorry, triangles, you've indicated the concentration spots. The -- taking first the area to the south. The concentration spots that you mentioned previously are located primarily upon -- along the Konjevic Polje-Kravica-Nova Kasaba road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Taking -- taking the information on this map, you have marked a few of these locations with red dots. Can you explain to the Court the distinction that you have made between the execution sites, the detention sites, and the mass execution sites. You've made a distinction between -- with your red dot and your red triangle, between an execution site and a mass execution site. Can you explain the difference?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's -- it's a difficult distinction to make. When we mark execution site, in fact we -- I spot -- I spot an area where we have reports that killings happened and -- at the place -- we call it -- we say small-scale killings. So the borderline is tricky between what we determine as being just an execution site or -- what was the other name on the other -- can I have the exhibit to the right. What is the name we use? Execution site and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And a mass execution site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've indicated mass execution sites with red dots.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's say that under 150 individuals - that is the scale of the Cerska Valley execution - we don't say that it's a mass execution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So with regard to the events after the fall of the enclave in Srebrenica, anything less than 150 is considered a small-scale execution?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. There are even several events we don't even talk about. If it is about individual murders or little groups, we would not even mention it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've also indicated on this map, Mr. Ruez, that there are primary mass graves that are undisturbed, primary mass graves that are disturbed, and secondary mass graves.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court the difference between the primary graves and the secondary graves.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The primary mass graves are the graves in which the bodies of those who have been recently executed have been buried into, after the execution. The secondary mass graves are the result of a disturbance process of the primary ones. The bodies were taken from these primary sites and then scattered in multiple graves, each of them being filled with an amount ranging between 80 and 180 individuals, in an obvious effort to scatter these crime scenes to make sure that we would not come across them. And if we would, that we would not be able to confirm the scale of the massacres as they were described by the victims or those who participated in it and talked about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I realise that there are witnesses who will come after you to go into detail concerning the secondary mass grave sites. However, I just wanted to ask you: As a part of your investigation, were you able to link the primary mass graves with the secondary mass graves which were subsequently discovered?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, as a part of your investigation, did you have the opportunity to interview several of the defendants in this particular case?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically with regard to Dragan Obrenovic, were you present when the interview of Mr. Obrenovic was conducted on April 2nd of 2000?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That we have labelled as Prosecution Exhibit 25.1. Exhibits 26.1 and 26.2 are interviews that were conducted with Dragan Jokic on December 14th, 1999 and April the 1st, 2000 respectively. Were you present when both of those interviews were conducted?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to the three interviews I've just mentioned, the one of Mr. Obrenovic and the two of Mr. Jokic, could you explain to the Court the process by which you obtained an interview with these accused?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The three suspects were summoned by the Prosecutor to appear for an interview at a determined place, date, and hour in Banja Luka. And this is what they did. They came to the appointment that was made with made with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did both Mr. Obrenovic and Mr. Jokic appear at their interviews voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They came accompanied with their Defence lawyer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, were both Mr. Obrenovic and Mr. Jokic read their rights?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As part of that particular recitation of their rights, were they told that they had a right not to answer any of the questions?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they also informed - and I believe you mentioned - that they had the right to have a Defence counsel present?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say, "He was present," did Mr. Jokic and Mr. Obrenovic have counsel present at the interview you conducted?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They apparently made the choice to have the same Defence lawyer, Mr. Simic, but he was present during all the time of the interviews with both of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Court the rest of the rights that you read to both Mr. Jokic and Mr. Obrenovic prior to beginning the interview.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The right to stay -- to be represented by a Defence lawyer, the right to stay silent, being informed that whatever they would say could be turned into evidence during proceedings in The Hague, the right to be assisted by an -- by an interpreter of their choice. They agreed to use the one we were offering them to use.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After having been read their rights, did both Mr. Obrenovic and Mr. Jokic agree to speak with you and other representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there an interpreter present to assist them and yourselves in translating from the Bosnian Serb language to English and back?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the course of the interview, did you give Mr. Obrenovic or Mr. Jokic a break if and when they requested?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. Yes. They could have requested a break at any moment, and we were offering breaks both for the sake of their rest and our rest, I would say, approximately every hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the interviews recorded?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout the interviews that were recorded with both Mr. Obrenovic and Mr. Jokic, was there ever a point in time when either indicated that they no longer wished to answer any questions?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any point in time, did anybody either on the audio cassette or outside of the taping at a break or any other time threaten or coerce Mr. Obrenovic or Mr. Jokic into speaking with you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given your experience as an investigator and the fact that you were present at both -- or excuse me, all three of these interviews, do you believe that both of these defendants gave interviews freely and voluntarily to the OTP back in 1999 and 2000?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I've also indicated previously that the Prosecutor has prepared identity books labelled "Prosecution Exhibit 22" which corresponds to the video that we watched earlier, as well as "Prosecution Exhibit 23," which is an identification book of the Muslims depicted in the videotape in Potocari. Have you reviewed both of those books?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you familiar with their contents?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with all of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had the opportunity to watch both the videotape and to look at the -- the identity books that the OTP has created?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything about those books that you have found to be inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. MS. DE LA TORRE: Your Honour, it's my understanding that the Court would prefer that we wait to tender any of the exhibits until after the redirect. That being said at this time, I would pass the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have about ten minutes left for today's hearing, so my suggestion is we will adjourn at this moment and tomorrow afternoon the Defence team will conduct the cross-examination. Is that agreeable to everybody? MS. DE LA TORRE: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And if I may make a minor request. I understand that the gentleman indicated that prior to coming here, he was provided with the questions to which he was supposed to answer by the Prosecution and he also has been looking at some material down there. I know we have been provided some material. If he would be so kind to provide us with a copy of those questions, I would most appreciate it, and anything else that he was referring to that has not been provided to us, because I have noticed that he's been looking down. I'm sure he's been testifying from his memory, but just to be on the safe side, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections? MS. DE LA TORRE: No, Your Honour. Just for the record, everything that's contained within the binder Defence counsel already has a copy of. We don't have any objection to their obtaining a copy of the final exhumation numbers and the outline of the crime scenes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, no -- well, the witness indicated that he has a kind of question outline. I would like to ask was he provided this kind of outlines? MS. DE LA TORRE: I'm sorry? You would like ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the witness indicated that in the binders he has a kind of outline of the questions which might be asked to him. I just want to ask: Who prepared this kind of outline? MS. DE LA TORRE: The outline of the crime scenes, as I indicated, that was prepared by myself, and we don't have any objection to providing that to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think, you know, Mr. Karnavas, your request is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just to make sure, the witness indicated that he had an outline of questions that he was going to be asked throughout his testimony. And if that is the case, I would -- that's what my understanding was. If I am mistaken, I stand corrected. But if that is the case, I would like to have the outline of the questions that were prepared by the Prosecution for the witness in preparation for his testimony that we've heard for the last three -- three sessions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is there any misunderstanding here? MS. DE LA TORRE: I don't believe so, Your Honour. We've already stated we have no objection to providing that to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe the registrar could have that list of the questions -- outline of the questions and furnish it to the Defence counsel, as well as to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excellent suggestion, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Wilson, are you going to conduct your cross-examination today or prefer to do it tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: My apologies. Your Honour, it was the agreement of the Defence at our scheduling conference before Judge Schomburg that we would proceed in the order of the indictment, so Mr. Blagojevic and his lawyer would go first. We would be second, and Mr. Jokic would be third, if that's agreeable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So tomorrow afternoon at 2.15 we'll resume in the same courtroom. We will rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 20th day of May, 2003, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.51 p.m.,
